asp.fluidez.nota:
Turn it down if opening the map costs you FPS in the game. No recorded
lap and no comparison accuracy is lost: the only change is that the
cars move in bigger steps.
avi.antelacion_nota: Measured in seconds and not metres because three hundred metres are not the same on a straight as into a hairpin. And it counts along the track, not as the crow flies: that way it does not warn about a car that is close but on the other side of a corner.
avi.colocar: While this window is open you will see the sign in grey over the game: drag it with the mouse to wherever you want it to appear.
avi.intro: A big sign over the game when there is a stopped car ahead. It is not the kind of spotter that warns you when it is already beside you: because the program knows where everyone is on the track, it warns while you can still do something about it.
avi.sonar: Play a beep with the warning
avi.sonido_nota:
IF YOU TEST IT AND NOTHING SOUNDS, it is almost certainly this: the beep goes out through the Windows DEFAULT device, not through wherever the game sounds. If the game is on a USB headset and the default is the monitor or the laptop speakers, the warning is sounding where you cannot hear it.
It is a quick fix: right-click the speaker in the taskbar, Sound settings, and set your headset as the default device. It does not affect the game.

It is a beep and not a voice on purpose: a voice has to be generated and that takes a good half second, which is exactly the time the warning was trying to buy you. To use your own, drop a .wav in the sonidos folder and it will show in the list.
avi.suena_por: The beep plays through the Windows default device
avi.texto_nota: Leave it empty for the usual text. If you write %d somewhere, the seconds left appear there: for example  CAR STOPPED IN %d s
ayuda.acerca:
What this is and who makes it.

LANGUAGE. Pick it from the list. The window that is already open
stays as it is; the change shows up completely next time you open
the program.

Each language is one file inside the idiomas folder. Anyone who
wants to translate into another language copies en.json, renames
it and translates; the program picks it up on its own.

DONATIONS. The program is free and is going to stay that way. The
buttons only appear if an account has been set in enlaces.py.

CLOSE THE MAP closes the whole program, not just this window.
ayuda.aspecto:
Size and colour of everything.

Your car is always drawn last and with a black ring, so even
when the dots pile up it is never covered.

Opacity affects the whole map: turn it down if it bothers you
while driving.
ayuda.avisos:
THE STOPPED CAR WARNING

A big sign appears over the game when someone is stopped on track ahead of you, as early as you decide.

IT IS NOT A SPOTTER
A spotter warns by proximity: it tells you there is someone beside you when they are already beside you. This is different. The program knows where every car is ON THE TRACK, so it can warn you while the stopped car is still ten seconds away, which is when you can still lift or change line.

WHY IN SECONDS
Because three hundred metres are not the same on the Le Mans straight as into a hairpin: there they are three seconds, here fifteen. The driver cares about seconds.

And it counts along the track, not as the crow flies. A car on the other side of a hairpin can be thirty metres away in a straight line and half a kilometre away on track: that is not a danger, and warning about it would be noise.

IT DOES NOT GET STUCK
It is recalculated twenty times a second. As soon as the car moves off, the warning goes away by itself. And so it does not flicker when the car sits right on the limit, once lit it holds for a moment and does not go out until the danger really moves away.

IF YOU CANNOT HEAR THE BEEP
The beep goes out through the Windows DEFAULT device, not through wherever the game sounds. With the game on a USB headset and the default set to the monitor, the warning sounds where you cannot hear it. Fix it from the speaker in the taskbar; it does not affect the game.

WHEN IT DOES NOT WARN
Below about 40 km/h it stays quiet: stopped in the pits or crawling along, everything is many seconds away and the warning would say nothing useful.
ayuda.coches:
Which car each one is driving.

THE PROGRAM WORKS IT OUT ON ITS OWN. When a session ends, Le Mans
Ultimate writes a file with the make and model of every car that was
out there. The program reads those files on startup and builds its
table from them. Nothing to type in.

The green line at the top shows what it has gathered: how many
different car models, how many liveries, and from how many sessions.

WHEN NEW CARS COME OUT they turn up on their own. Just run a session
with them on track: once it ends they are identified. The "Read the
cars from the game" button forces that read if you do not want to wait
for the next startup.

CARS THE GAME HAS, at the bottom, is the list of models it has found,
by category. That is the list the Setups tab will use.

NOT IDENTIFIED only shows a car that has not finished a single session
yet. You can fill it in by hand if you are in a hurry, but it sorts
itself out as soon as you finish a race with it.

WHY THE TEAM NAME IS NOT ENOUGH. A real team races in several classes
at once: United Autosports runs a McLaren in GT3 and an Oreca in LMP2.
That is why each car is identified by its code, not by the team name.
And online, on top of that, every player gives their car whatever team
name they like.

LMP2 cars are all Oreca 07 and the program already knows that.
ayuda.escaneo:
This is where tracks get measured. They come measured from the
factory, and you only need to scan if a new track comes out, if
an existing one changes, or if you see that one is wrong.

YOU DO NOT NEED TO PICK ANYTHING IN THE LIST TO SCAN. The three
buttons at the bottom measure the track YOU ARE ON INSIDE THE
GAME at that moment. The list is only for looking at how the
scans came out and for deleting them.

THE LIST. It shows every layout you have installed, with their
variants: Silverstone has four, Paul Ricard five. The three
columns say what has been measured on each. If a game update
brings a new track, it appears on its own.
   View the scan  - draws it in a window so you can check it did
                    not come out crooked (or double click)
   Refresh        - reads the list again. Use it after scanning
                    something, to see it reflected
   Delete         - throws away everything measured for that
                    layout

THE THREE SCANS, in this order:

1. OUTLINE. Do 3 laps SLOWLY and DOWN THE MIDDLE of the road. It
   draws wherever you go, so if you take the racing line the map
   comes out deformed. Do not go into the pits. The corner
   numbers and names come from this too.

2. EDGES. One lap with the LEFT wheel on the white line and
   another with the RIGHT one, slowly and without lifting it off.
   The program tells you which is which as you go. This is what
   draws the track at its real width, which you need in order to
   compare lines.

3. PITS. Leave the pits, do one transition lap, and at the end of
   it come into the pits and drive the whole lane down the middle
   without stopping, until you are back out on track. It starts
   and stops recording on its own, because the game does say when
   you are in the pit lane.

IF YOU SCAN SOMETHING THAT WAS ALREADY MEASURED, the program
warns you and asks before replacing it. Redoing the outline does
NOT wipe the edges or the pit lane: those are separate
measurements and still stand. Redoing the outline does recalculate
the corners.

In all three cases a black window opens with step-by-step
instructions. Do not close it until it finishes.
ayuda.fuerzas:
THE G FORCE BALL

The dot leans towards wherever the weight of the car is going: up under braking, down on the throttle, outwards in corners. In the centre, the car is balanced.

SENSITIVITY

How many G it takes for the dot to reach the edge of the circle. The lower it is, the more the dot moves. At 2.5 G an LMP2 only touches the edge under heavy braking and in fast corners (measured on track). For a slower car, lower it.

SMOOTHING

The game publishes G forces with every kerb strike in them, and at twenty frames per second the dot shakes too much to read while driving. Smoothing makes the dot chase the reading instead of jumping to it.

THE NUMBERS

They are the real weight balance, measured at the four wheels. Note it is not 50/50: a running LMP2 almost always carries more weight at the rear (about two thirds mid-corner) because of aerodynamic load. That is normal.

PLACING IT

With this window open, drag the ball anywhere with the mouse.
ayuda.parados:
Cars stopped or nearly stopped out on track flash on the map and
are drawn bigger.

It is mainly for blind corners: you see where the stopped car is
before you get there, instead of finding it.

WHY THE YELLOW FLAG IS NOT USED: a whole session was recorded to
check, and LMU does not publish flags to external programs. Not
the game phase, not the yellow flag state, not each car's status
- none of them ever change even when the flag is on screen. So
the program does not wait for the game to tell it: it looks for
the stopped car directly, which is the real danger flag or no
flag.

It has to be below 40 km/h for several readings in a row, so a
car that simply brakes hard is not flagged. Cars going slowly
down the pit lane are never flagged.
ayuda.reglajes:
SORT OUT MY SETUPS opens the library, and that part does work.

It reads every setup you have in the game, tells you which car each
one is for and what it is for, and flags the ones that are short on
fuel.

SHORT ON FUEL is the important warning. LMU has two tanks: virtual
energy, which is the big bar you see in the garage, and fuel, which
is separate. Many qualifying setups load fuel for a lap and a half
while the bar promises six laps. The car dies on track with no
warning at all. The FIX THE FUEL button gives it what it needs, and
saves a copy of the original before touching anything.

RENAME gives them a name you can read, with the car first:
LexusRCF_Dry_Race_Safe_GO_V141. It is needed because the game lists
every setup in the track folder without checking which car it is
for, and will happily load a Lexus setup on a Ford.

IMPORT takes loose .svm files and also the zip exactly as you
download it, with the whole pack inside.

COMPARE two setups tells you how they differ, in plain words and with
the important things first. Pick two from the list holding Ctrl.

THE CAR IS DOING SOMETHING ODD is the engineer. You say where it
happens, what it does and when, and it tells you what to change and
why. Change ONE thing at a time; the result is saved as a new file
and the old one is left alone.

LEARN FROM MY SETUPS reads everything you have and works out the
sensible step for each adjustment on YOUR cars. The more good setups
you have, the better it gets. It stores numbers, not setups.

----------

What is below DOES NOT WORK YET: it is a preview of how it will
look, which is why it is greyed out with the COMING SOON stamp.

FEATURES tells you what each car is: its engine, capacity, power,
whether the engine sits at the front, in the middle or hangs out the
back, and which wheels it drives.

SETUP shows the same pages the game has under PIT GARAGE -> CAR
SETUP, with the same names, so you know exactly where to look.

THE SETUP MANUAL is the other half: the engineer tells you WHAT to change, and the manual explains WHY and what it costs. It covers all one hundred garage settings one by one, recipes sorted by what the car is doing, and sections by class, by car and by track. Shortcut: in the editor, clicking a setting's NAME opens the manual at its page. (The manual itself is in Spanish for now.)

THE MANUAL HAS TWO VOLUMES: SETUPS (what to change in the garage) and DRIVING (what to do at the wheel) - seating position, technique corner by corner, common mistakes, endurance racing and multiclass traffic, plus sections by class, by car and by track. Switch volumes with the buttons at the top of the window.
ayuda.salidas:
Marks with a triangle where you last went off track at that
point.

The warning clears itself as soon as you go through cleanly
again, and is replaced if you go off there once more.

Three signals are used: the game invalidating your lap (practice
and qualifying), the game penalising you (in the race it does not
invalidate, it penalises) and the program's own detection by
position. If you tick the box, only the game is listened to and
you get no warning for anything it lets go.
ayuda.tiempos:
Measures you against the fastest lap of the rivals.

The track is painted in the colour of the reference, and your
own segments are laid over it: red where you are slower, yellow
where you match and green where you are beating him.

Your segments are NOT wiped when you cross the line: each one
keeps the last time you went through there. And if a rival
improves, your whole lap recolours itself against the new mark.

Only laps driven with the program open count: the game publishes
each car's best LAP TIME, but not how fast it was at each point,
so an earlier lap cannot be reconstructed.
ayuda.trazadas:
Compare your line with the fastest car's.

A window opens with the recorded sessions. Pick one and you get
the list of your laps with their times and sectors: the best lap
in green and the best time in each sector in blue.

You can select SEVERAL laps at once with Ctrl. It is for what
usually happens: on one lap you were good in sector 1 and on
another in sector 3; seeing them together shows the lap that
ought to be there.

The track is drawn at its real width, and your line is coloured
against the reference just like on the map: red slower, yellow
the same, green faster.

The mouse wheel zooms and dragging moves it. The button to
delete sessions is in there too, so your disk does not fill up.
ayuda.ver:
What gets drawn on top of the track.

Corner numbers are counted from the start/finish line. The names
come from the program's own database; not every track has them,
and on those you will only see the number.
bib.asignado_ayuda:
THE COLOURS IN THE LIST

GREEN AND BOLD, with an arrow: the setup the game will load NOW, on the track and with the car you are on. There can only be one.

MUTED GREEN: other setups you have assigned, for other tracks or other cars. The game keeps one per combination, so if you have raced on six tracks you will have six. You are not using them: they load when you go to that track with that car.

WHERE THIS COMES FROM

The game does not record anywhere the setup you LOAD in the garage. It was checked step by step: loading leaves no trace, going out on track neither, changing session neither.

The only thing the game writes, and instantly, is the setup you ASSIGN: on the setups screen, the ASSIGN button next to LOAD.

And to know which one is the here-and-now, the game has to be open, because it is the game that says which track you are on and with which car. With the game closed it cannot be known, and then it says so instead of pointing at one at random.

CAREFUL, ASSIGNING DOES SOMETHING ELSE TOO

Besides writing it down, assigning a setup makes the game load it automatically next time you enter that track with that car. Some people want that and some do not, so it is your call.

This program only READS that file. It never assigns anything itself and never changes it.

A COPY leaves the old setup as it was and creates a new one next to it. Good when you are trying something and not sure.

fov.aviso_pulgadas: This is approximate: the diagonal quoted by manufacturers sometimes includes a bit of bezel. If you can, measure the lit area with a tape.
fov.consejos:
TIPS
Measure the picture only, edge to edge of the area that lights up. Black bezels do not count.
Distance is measured from your eyes, sitting in your driving position, to the centre of the screen.
In Le Mans Ultimate the setting is the VERTICAL FOV: use the big number.
You change it inside the car, in the camera or seat options.
A correct FOV feels odd for the first few days: it seems faster and you seem to see less. That is exactly what you were missing. Give it three or four runs before you judge it.
fov.desde_pulgadas: Do not know the width and height? Work them out from the inches
fov.dist_pista: from your eyes to the centre of the screen (cm)
fov.error: Check the numbers: all three must be greater than zero.
fov.formula:
THE MATHS
Vertical FOV = 2 x arctangent( height / (2 x distance) )
Horizontal FOV = 2 x arctangent( width / (2 x distance) )
fov.sub: Measure your screen and how far your eyes are from it. The result updates as you type.
fov.tres_pantallas:
IF YOU RUN TRIPLE SCREENS
The vertical FOV does not change: it is the one shown here, using the height of ONE screen and your distance.
What changes is the horizontal angle, and the game handles that once you turn on triple screen mode and tell it the angle of the side screens.

ing.y_si_no_texto:
This screen will always give you an answer, and that is the trap: it makes it look like anything the car does can be fixed by changing the setup. Often it cannot.

Here is the sum real engineers do: a good setup is worth TENTHS a lap. Driving is worth SECONDS. So if you have been stuck on the same lap time for a while, those seconds are far more likely to be in how you drive the lap than in the anti-roll bar.

And this is not about being able to drive or not. It happens to everyone, and it happens most of all with a new car: everyone brakes in a different place, turns in differently and puts up with different things. A setup that works beautifully for another driver can be awful for you simply because he enters the corner another way.


THE TEST THAT SETTLES IT

Run five laps back to back and look at the times.

If they are far apart, half a second or more, the car is not the problem yet. What is missing is repeating: same braking point, same turn-in, same throttle. Once the laps start to look alike, the setup will show. Not before, because every lap you are asking the car for something different and no setup covers all of them.

If they come out close together and you still lack pace, then it is time. The car is doing the same thing every lap, you can say with confidence what it does, and this screen will genuinely help.


THE OTHER SIGN

If the car does something different every lap in the same corner, no setup will fix that.

If it does the same thing, in the same place, at the same moment, then it is the car. And that is what this is for.


One last thing: a new car means starting over. A GT3 and a Hypercar do not drive alike at all, and in the first hours with a new one being slow is the normal outcome. Give it time before you blame the setup.

reg.res.911gt3r:
Engine hung out behind the rear axle: huge traction out of slow
corners, but overdo the braking and that weight pushes the tail
round. Brake in a straight line, then turn.
reg.res.992spc:
A single-make cup car, with no ABS and no traction control. Pure
schooling: brake crooked and it is gone.
reg.res.adessad25:
Engine shared by the whole LMP3 class. Chassis with little
downforce: you drive it with the wheel, not with the aero.
reg.res.alpinea424:
LMDh with a small engine and a lot of turbo. It pulls late
but very hard up top. Kind front end, leans on the track
nicely through medium corners.
reg.res.astonmartinvalkyrie:
The only one with no hybrid and no turbo. Instant
throttle response and real engine braking, but it
loses out of slow corners against the hybrids.
Sensitive to roll.
reg.res.astonmartinvantageamr:
The previous Vantage GT3. Friendly at the rear,
tends to understeer if you load the nose too much.
reg.res.bmwm4lmgt3:
Front engine, but set well back. Neutral and easy to read, and
it looks after its tyres. It is the car in the screenshots used
as the example on this page.
reg.res.bmwmhybridv8:
LMDh with plenty of torque down low. The rear steps out if
you open the throttle early; wants a soft diff and some wing.
reg.res.cadillacv_lmdh:
Very linear delivery, easy to meter out. One of the
friendliest in the class, and its bodywork copes well
in the tow.
reg.res.chevroletc8rlm:
A mid-engined GTE. More downforce and less weight than a
GT3: everything happens faster, and mistakes cost you
sooner.
reg.res.corvettez06gt3r:
Naturally aspirated, so the response is direct. Brakes
very hard and is stable, but the nose feels heavy in slow
corners.
reg.res.duqueined09lmp3:
Same engine as the rest of LMP3. A bit more settled at
the rear than the Ligier, a little lazier at the nose.
reg.res.ferrari296gt3:
Mid engine: it turns beautifully and changes direction very
quickly. In exchange, it is easy to overrotate through linked
corners.
reg.res.ferrari488gtelm:
A GTE honed over years of development. Quick-responding
turbo and excellent traction.
reg.res.ferrari499p:
LMH with an electric motor on the front axle: above 190 km/h
it drives all four wheels. Very strong out of fast corners,
a little lazy at the nose in the slow ones.
reg.res.fordmustanggt3:
Heavy at the nose and very friendly. Forgives mistakes, but
punishes the front tyres over a long stint.
reg.res.genesisgmr001:
The newest car on the grid. Neutral behaviour, no quirks,
a good base for learning the class.
reg.res.ginettag61evo:
An LMP3 with slow reactions that forgives a lot. A good
choice to start out in prototypes.
reg.res.isottatipo6:
A heavy LMH with less downforce than the rest. Needs a soft
setup so it does not chew the tyres.
reg.res.lamborghinihuracangt3:
One of the fastest through corners in the class. Very
direct, and it wants precision: any correction at the
wheel costs you time.
reg.res.lamborghinisc63:
Nervous on turn-in, oversteers if you release the brake
abruptly. Better with the rear bar loose.
reg.res.lexusrcfgt3:
Naturally aspirated front engine with the smoothest delivery
of all. Very good on worn tyres and in the wet.
reg.res.ligierjsp325:
The liveliest of the LMP3s. Turns in very well but wants a
careful right foot.
reg.res.mclaren720sgchallenge:
The circuit version of the road car, with more power
and less downforce than the GT3. Very quick in a
straight line, demands a lot under braking.
reg.res.mclaren720sgt3evo:
Mid-engined turbo with a lot of downforce. It flies
through fast corners; in the slow ones you have to wait
for the turbo before opening up.
reg.res.mercedesamggt3evo:
The class classic. Big, smooth engine and stable,
predictable behaviour at all times.
reg.res.oreca07elms:
Single-make: everyone runs the same car, the difference is
only the setup and the driver. Huge downforce for its weight,
and it brakes brutally well.
reg.res.oreca07lm:
The WEC version of the Oreca 07, with a bit more power. Same
behaviour: enormous through fast corners, delicate in the slow
ones if you abuse the kerbs.
reg.res.peugeot9x8:
LMH with a front hybrid. Very particular aero: it lives off
ride height, and any change shows up far more than on the
others.
reg.res.porsche911rsr_19:
Careful: this 911 carries its engine IN FRONT of the rear
axle, not behind it. It behaves like a mid-engined car,
nothing like the 911 GT3 R in the GT3 class.
reg.res.porsche963:
One of the most balanced. Brakes very late and looks after
its tyres over a long stint.
reg.res.sgc007:
LMH with no hybrid, of an older design. Little downforce: fast
on the straights, struggles through linked corners.
reg.res.toyotagr10:
LMH with a front hybrid. The most polished in the class:
stable, predictable and very good in the wet thanks to AWD.
reg.res.vandervell680:
LMH with no hybrid and no aids. Hard work to drive, chews
the rear tyres; rewards anyone clean with the throttle.
reg.res.vantageamrgt3evo:
Updated Vantage. Plenty of torque down low, so be smooth
with the throttle on exit; very stable under braking.
reg.v.trasera_hibrido_delantero_4x4_a_al: Rear-wheel drive + front hybrid (AWD at speed)
sc.abre_lmu: Open LMU and get on track before launching this.
sc.bo.como:
1. Leave the pits and do one transition lap to get set.
  2. As you cross the line, start the LEFT SIDE lap: the left
     wheel on the white line, slowly, without lifting it off at
     any point.
  3. When you cross the line again, do another transition lap.
  4. As you cross the line, do the RIGHT SIDE lap, the same but
     with the right wheel on the line.
  5. Cross the line and it finishes and saves on its own.
sc.bo.corta: Lap too short (%d points). Do this lap again.
sc.bo.cuidado:
CAREFUL: that width is not normal. One of the laps may not
  have followed the line. It is worth redoing the scan.
sc.bo.despacio: (you are doing %.0f km/h: slower, precision is being lost)
sc.bo.faltan_lados: Sides are still missing. Nothing is saved.
sc.bo.fase_derecha: RIGHT SIDE. Right wheel on the line, slowly.
sc.bo.fase_izquierda: LEFT SIDE. Left wheel on the line, slowly.
sc.bo.fase_transicion: TRANSITION LAP. Get set and head for the line.
sc.bo.sin_trazado:
CAREFUL: this track has no outline yet. Scan the OUTLINE
first and repeat this scan afterwards.
sc.bo.ya_escaneado: This track ALREADY HAS its edges scanned.
sc.bx.como:
1. Leave the pits and do one transition lap.
  2. At the end of that lap, ENTER the pits.
  3. Drive the whole lane down the middle, without stopping.
  4. Go back out on track and it saves on its own.
sc.bx.cuidado:
CAREFUL: that is very short for a pit lane.
  You may not have driven all of it. Worth doing again.
sc.bx.dentro:
>>> IN THE PITS. Drive the whole lane down the middle,
    without stopping, until you are back out on track.
sc.bx.empieza: >>> Do your transition lap and enter the pits whenever you like.
sc.bx.has_salido: You have left the pits. %d points recorded.
sc.bx.muy_poco:
Exit detected with only %d points: far too few.
    Go back in and drive the whole lane.
sc.bx.sin_trazado:
This track has no outline yet.
Scan the OUTLINE first and repeat this afterwards.
sc.bx.ya_escaneado: This track ALREADY HAS its pit lane scanned.
sc.cancelado_ctrlc: Scan cancelled. Nothing has been saved.
sc.cerrar: Press ENTER to close this window...
sc.sin_coches: No cars in the session. Get on track and try again.
sc.sin_coches2: No cars in the session. Get on track first.
sc.sin_jugador: I cannot identify your car in the session.
sc.tz.instrucciones:
- Do %d laps of the track.
  - Go SLOWLY and down the MIDDLE of the road: it draws
    wherever you go, so the racing line deforms the map.
  - Do NOT enter the pits or reset the car mid-lap.
  - To stop early, press Ctrl+C.
sc.tz.largo: It measures %.1f m according to the game.
sc.tz.ninguna_entera:
No lap is complete. Try doing another lap in one go,
without going back to the pits or resetting the car.
sc.tz.otra_variante:
There was already a layout saved under this name but it measures %.0f m,
and this one is %.0f m: they are two different variants. Both are kept
and the program will pick the right one for each race.
sc.tz.pocos_puntos: Too few points (%d). At least one full lap is needed.
sc.tz.se_sustituye: The OUTLINE will be replaced and the corners detected again.
sc.tz.vuelta_usada: lap used     : %d   (loop closes with %.1f m of error)
sc.tz.ya_escaneado: This track HAS ALREADY BEEN SCANNED.
sc.tz.ya_puedes: You can now open the map on this track.
sel.ayuda: The game does not always say which car you are driving: as a spectator, or when you take over in a driver swap, it says nothing. Pick your car here and the map will follow it even when the driver changes. While the car is not confirmed the map warns you and saves no laps as yours.
sel.nadie: nobody (the map does not know which one you are)
tie.activado:
Right now: ON. The track is painted in the reference colour with
your own segments over it in red, yellow and green.
tie.apagado:
Right now: OFF. The track is drawn grey. Press the button above
to turn it on.
tie.avisar_parados: Warn about stopped cars on track
tie.avisar_salidas: Mark where I went off track
tie.buscar_avisos: Search for the game's warning counter (diagnostics)
tie.nota_banderas:
LMU does not publish flags to external programs, so the
stopped car itself is detected instead. Press the i.
tie.solo_juego: Only when the game penalises me
tra.intro:
Recorded automatically while you drive with the map open: for
each of your laps the line, the time and the three sectors, and
the fastest lap of the rivals.
tra.resumen:
%d sessions saved, %.0f KB in total.
Latest: %s, %s, %d laps.
ver.anillo: My car as a ring (lets you see who is alongside)
vis.como_va:
ONE of your laps selected: it is painted red, yellow and green against the rival.
SEVERAL selected: each one in its own colour, to see where each one goes.
vis.confirmar_borrar:
This will be deleted:

%s  %s  (%d laps, %.0f KB)

This cannot be undone.
vis.elige_sesion: Pick a session from the list
vis.elige_sesion_borrar: Pick a session from the list first.
vis.ley_marca_algo: select something in the list on the left
vis.ley_una_sola: select just one to see where you gain and lose
vis.no_se_lee: That session could not be read.
vis.que_dibujar: What to draw  (pick several with Ctrl)
vis.sin_bordes: This track has no EDGES scanned: only the line is drawn, without track width.
vis.sin_mias: None of your laps were recorded in this session.
vis.sin_rival: No rival completed a full lap while the program was open, so there is nothing to compare against.
vis.sin_sesiones:

vis.sin_trazado: The outline of this track is not saved.
